title: Forecasting Slab Capacity and Token Cost Models
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet defines a "slab" approach to capacity planning (Reserved / Spot / Burst slabs) and produces a simple, region-aware $/1M tokens mapping for planning and cash forecasting. The goal is to give product and finance a single, interpretable number per region to use in P&L scenarios while preserving the ability to tune utilization, slab-mix, and model-level throughput.

Key ideas and definitions:
- Slab: a homogeneous group of GPU capacity procured and billed under a common contract and cost profile. We use three slabs:
  1) Reserved slab: committed instances (monthly or annual), lowest $/GPU-hour but requires utilization to be amortized.
  2) Spot slab: preemptible/market instances, deep discount but availability varies.
  3) Burst slab: on-demand / cloud-managed autoscale capacity, highest $/GPU-hour used for peak SLOs.
- Tokens-per-GPU-hour: model + config specific. For modeling we track two representative workloads: "midweight-chat" (approx. M tokens/hr) and "embed-heavy" (lower per-token compute).
- Effective $/1M tokens = (effective_gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_gpu_hour) * 1e6. Effective_gpu_hour_cost accounts for utilization and overheads (infra, networking, maintenance).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Reference GPU: A100/40GB equivalent on average.
- Overhead multiplier (infra + storage + misc) = 1.08x on top of raw instance cost.
- Baseline tokens per GPU-hour by workload:
    midweight-chat: 250M tokens / GPU-hour (single-model optimized, decoding-heavy, quantized kernels)
    embed-heavy: 800M tokens / GPU-hour (dense compute; batching-friendly)
- Utilization factors: Reserved slab expected util = 78% baseline (smoothing + caching), Spot slab util = 60% effective (due to preemptions & warm-up), Burst slab util = 35% (short-lived, tail latency constraints).

Formulas used:
- effective_gpu_hour_cost = raw_instance_hour_cost * overhead_multiplier / utilization_factor
- $/1M tokens = (effective_gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_gpu_hour) * 1_000_000

Example regional cost table (raw_instance_hour_cost = cloud list price for a reference GPU; numbers are rounded):

CSV: region, slab, raw_hour_cost, overhead_multiplier, util, eff_hour_cost, tokens_per_gpu_hour, $/1M_tokens

"us-west-2",Spot,0.70,1.08,0.60,1.26,250000000,5.04
"us-west-2",Burst,2.50,1.08,0.35,7.71,250000000,30.84

"us-east-1",Reserved,1.75,1.08,0.78,2.42,250000000,9.68
"us-east-1",Spot,0.68,1.08,0.60,1.22,250000000,4.88
"us-east-1",Burst,2.45,1.08,0.35,7.55,250000000,30.20

"eu-west-1",Reserved,1.90,1.08,0.78,2.63,250000000,10.52
"eu-west-1",Spot,0.78,1.08,0.60,1.40,250000000,5.60
"eu-west-1",Burst,2.80,1.08,0.35,8.66,250000000,34.64

"asia-east-1",Burst,3.50,1.08,0.35,10.80,250000000,43.20

Notes on numbers: raw_hour_costs are market-average public-cloud references for a single A100-equivalent GPU; reserved is the amortized committed price we currently expect in each region. Spot estimates are historical average market prices. Burst equals on-demand list. Tokens_per_gpu_hour used above = midweight-chat baseline (250M).

Embed-heavy example (same region mapping but tokens_per_gpu_hour = 800M):
- us-west-2 Reserved $/1M tokens = (2.49/800M)*1e6 = 3.11
- us-west-2 Spot $/1M tokens = 1.26/800M*1e6 = 1.57
- us-west-2 Burst $/1M tokens = 7.71/800M*1e6 = 9.64

Sensitivity analysis (short notes):
- Utilization swing: reserved slab utilization +/-10ppt changes reserved $/1M tokens by roughly +/-1.3–1.6$ depending on region. This is the largest lever for near-term unit economics.
- Slab mix: moving 10% of sustained traffic from reserved to spot reduces blended $/1M by ~0.5–1.2$ depending on region because spot is significantly cheaper even after preemption overhead.
- Model throughput improvements: a 15% throughput improvement (better batching/quant kernels) directly reduces $/1M by 15% across slabs. Prioritize compiler/kernel efforts for midweight-chat.

Blended planning table (example for us-west-2, baseline traffic mix = 70% reserved, 20% spot, 10% burst):
- blended_eff_hour_cost = 0.7*2.49 + 0.2*1.26 + 0.1*7.71 = 2.95 $/GPU-hour effective
- blended $/1M tokens (midweight) = (2.95/250M)*1e6 = 11.80 $/1M tokens
- blended $/1M tokens (embed) = (2.95/800M)*1e6 = 3.69 $/1M tokens

Operational implications and SLO alignment:
- We should reserve capacity so that 60–75% of predictable baseline is covered by reserved slab; remainder handled by spot/burst to meet tail SLOs. This yields best blended economics while preserving high availability.
- For customers with strict latency SLAs, pin routes to private/dedicated clusters and charge a latency premium; treat those as dedicated-reserved-only in the slab model.
- Warm pools and rapid rehydration (spot fallback to burst) can meaningfully increase effective spot utilization; model this as +10–15ppt effective util on spot for services that implement it.

Planned capacity additions and burn forecast (Q1–Q3 2026):
- 2026-01: +120 GPUs reserved (us-east backbone), targeted to reduce reserved $/1M by ~0.3$.
- 2026-03: +80 GPUs spot (asia-east burst buffer). Expected to absorb 20% of peak traffic in APAC.
- 2026-06: +200 GPUs reserved (multi-region), funding contingent on top-line.
Forecasted GPU-hour burn (baseline month after additions): ~320k GPU-hours/month across infra, producing ~80B midweight-chat tokens / month under the current slab mix (baseline).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run token-per-GPU-hour microbenchmarks across the new kernel patches (Zoe) and update tokens_per_gpu_hour table. (action: Zoe, due 2026-03-20)
- Validate reserved pricing for new multi-region commit — finance needs final quotes (action: Marco).
- Add a separate sheet mapping customer-tier (free/standard/enterprise) to expected slab allocation and per-route $/1M token surcharge.

Appendix: quick modeling checklist for simulations
- Inputs: per-region raw list prices, slab mix targets, expected utilization by slab, tokens_per_gpu_hour by model class, overhead multiplier.
- Outputs: blended effective $/GPU-hour, $/1M tokens by model class, monthly GPU-hour burn, monthly token volume, total cost.
- Sensitivity runs recommended: util +/- 10ppt, tokens_per_gpu_hour +/- 10–20%, slab-mix +/- 10ppt.

This doc is intended as an operationally actionable compact model rather than a canonical econometrics study. Use it for stakeholder planning, finance forecasts, and quick trade-off decisioning.
